messages:
anya: Quick bakeoff recap — ran GPTQ trials across Llama-2-13b, Mistral-7b-v0.1, and Qwen-7b using our standard eval harness. Short summary up front: accuracy deltas vary by task, Mistral shows the smallest LMScore loss at 4-bit GPTQ, Qwen has a small but consistent numeracy regression, and Llama shows throughput wins but some KV-cache weirdness. Full artifacts in s3://redwood-ml/quant-bake/4301122334/

anya: Configs tested: GPTQ-4 (group_size=128, act-order), GPTQ-4 (group_size=64), GPTQ-8, and AWQ-4 for a couple baseline comparisons. All runs used our inference profile: seq=512, batch=1 for latency, and synthetic throughput runs with batching up to 8.

anya: Key metrics (highlight):
- Mistral-7b-v0.1 GPTQ-4 (gs128): LMScore delta ~ -0.9% vs fp16; latency +18% but throughput per-GPU ~ +22%
- Qwen-7b GPTQ-4 (gs128): LMScore delta ~ -2.7% on math/numeracy sets; hallucination rates slightly up on long-context summarization
- Llama-2-13b GPTQ-4 (gs64): LMScore delta ~ -1.5%; observed intermittent KV cache misses leading to token jitter in some streams

anya: Notable qualitative finds:
- Mistral preserved instruction-following better than expected for a 4-bit config.
- Qwen's tokenizer + quantized weights produced subtle probability mass shift on digits — manifests as off-by-one in arithmetic tasks.
- Llama 13b: when we switched act-order vs default ordering we saw different sampling modes causing divergence in regeneration tests.

matt: awesome, thanks. can you drop the exact command lines + eval IDs? want to re-run the failing numeracy case locally.

anya: pasted the quant command we used:
```
python tools/gptq_quantize.py \n  --model checkpoints/mistral-7b \n  --bits 4 \n  --group-size 128 \n  --act-order True \n  --save quant/mistral-7b-gptq4-gs128
```
All eval IDs are in the S3 folder under /evals/ with a small README.

bakebot: run complete: job=4301122334-gptq-sweep, artifacts uploaded, meta.json -> s3://redwood-ml/quant-bake/4301122334/meta.json :white_check_mark:

eva: saw the numeracy diffs. I pushed a short breakdown (per-dataset) to the bucket — link in the README. My hypothesis: Qwen's embedding scale interacts with per-channel quant noise. Tried per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric quantization in a quick test; asymmetric reduced the delta by ~0.6 percentage points.

srinivasan: interesting re: asymmetric — did you try OP-level reordering for the matmul kernel? that can affect effective quant noise when activation distributions are skewed.

eva: not in that quick pass, just toggled per-channel. I can queue a targeted run with OP reorder on the next slot.

kyle: for the Llama KV cache jitter, any pattern on sequence length or whether it's from persistent cache reuse (dedicated session) vs fresh sessions? saw a similar issue in previous GPTQ experiments.

anya: good call — it reproduces more when we do multi-turn streaming with cache reuse across multiple prompts (seqs with reused prefixes). Single-shot runs don't show it. Suspect packing of KV tensors during the quant pipeline introduced a rounding mismatch.

matt: can we add a quick regression test to our smoke harness that simulates multi-turn reuse? if it catches this early we can gate deploys to Dedicated.

ops-bot: created ticket INF-9876 "GPTQ KV cache jitter - Llama 13b" and assigned to eng-runtime -> https://jira.redwood.internal/INF-9876

anya: notes + recommendations:
- Short term: mark Qwen GPTQ-4 as "experimental" for numeracy-heavy routes; recommend AWQ-4 for user-facing math tasks until we fix tokenization/scale mismatch.
- For Llama-13b, disable session reuse for GPTQ-4 profiles until we pin the KV pack/align fix. Add a canary that runs multi-turn regen against a small prompt set.
- Mistral-7b: safe to promote to "recommended" for latency-sensitive routes with a note about slight throughput/latency tradeoffs.
- Ops: add a dedicated nightly job that re-runs the top-10 eval prompts under quant profiles and alerts on >1.0% LMScore regression.

matt: +1 to the nightly job. also would like a short blurb for docs/console with per-model deployment knobs (batching, session reuse toggle, quant-profile tag).

anya: drafting the docs blurb now, will push a PR to docs repo and link from the S3 README. ETA this afternoon.

srinivasan: can someone add the kernel/profile logs (perf counters) from the runs? I want to compare matmul tiling footprints across models to see if we can tune group_size per-arch.

anya: yes — added perf dumps under s3://redwood-ml/quant-bake/4301122334/perf/ (contains kernel logs, nvprof snippets, and CORES usage).

kyle: final ask: list of priority next steps so PM/eng-sre can act?

anya: prioritized list in the README: [1] AWQ fallback path for numeracy routes (Qwen), [2] fix KV pack alignment + add multi-turn canary (Llama), [3] OP reorder + asymmetric quant test (Qwen), [4] promote Mistral-4 to recommended with caveats, [5] nightly alert job and console flag for session reuse.

matt: perfect. thanks everyone — I'll start the PR for the console toggle and link back here once ready.

eva: I'll queue the OP reorder runs and tag results in the bucket.

anya: thanks — closing thread after I push docs. will update INF-9876 with findings. :rocket:
